chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Safwan ibn Yahya, who said:

I said to al-Rida عليه السلام: We used to ask you before Allah had granted Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام to you, and you would say: Allah will grant me a boy. Now Allah has indeed granted him to you, and He has delighted our eyes. May Allah not show us your day. But if an event should occur, then to whom? So he pointed with his hand to Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام, while he was standing before him.
So I said: May I be your ransom, this is a son of three years. He said: And what harm is there in that? ‘Isa عليه السلام stood with the hujjah while he was a son of three years.

key_terms.أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام, identified here as the successor
key_terms.الرِّضَا: Imam al-Rida عليه السلام, the speaker being addressed in the narration
key_terms.بِالْحُجَّةِ: with the divine proof or authority from Allah
key_terms.عِيسَى: Prophet ‘Isa عليه السلام, cited as a precedent for divine authority in childhood
key_terms.غُلَامًا: a boy; the child whom Allah granted to Imam al-Rida عليه السلام
key_terms.يَوْمَكَ: your day; a respectful reference to the day of passing away

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith show the Imamate of Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام despite his young age?
ai.summary: This hadith records a clear designation of Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام by al-Rida عليه السلام as the Imam after him. It also affirms that young age does not prevent divine authority, citing ‘Isa عليه السلام as one who stood with the hujjah while still very young.
